sources: Ó hÓgain, Dáithí. Myth, Legend and Romance: An Encyclopedia of the Irish Folk Tradition. New York: Prentice-Hall Press, 1991, 259.

text: Íte, also written Itta, Íta, Mo-Íde, or Míde, was an Irish saint. She lived as a Christian woman in the sixth century. Her legends hold many pagan motifs. She founded a convent at Cill Íte, now Killeedy in County Limerick. Much like the Kildare nun Brigit, she seems almost mythological. Her name may belong to a goddess with whom she merged. Her room shone as if on fire. She cured a man by taking away his horse's ears. Above all, she owned the Cow of Abundance, the Glas Ghaibhleann.
